description: I AM INTERESTED IN VIDEO GAMES
summary: mars resource lab is a junior astronaut mission trainer built in minecraft education. players land on a mars world generated from nasa mola elevation data , explore mesas , craters and ice , and collect raw materials. back at a solar powered base , they use chemistry blocks to break materials into elements and build compounds , keeping oxygen , water , power and food above zero. reduced gravity and limited sunlight change every decison. our map engine turns any planet's elevation image into a playable world , so the trainer can grow from mars to the moon , mercury and venus. kids and adults learn physics , chemistry and resource planning by playng.
details:
what it does: mars resource lab is a survival and resource management game that trains players like junior astronauts. the player lands on a mars world , explores real terrain , collects ice and ore , and processes them in a chemistry lab on a solar powered base. the goal is to keep four stocks above zero: oxygen , water , power and food. every trip outside spends them and every sucessful lab recipe refils them.

how it works: a python tool reads a grayscale mola elevation image from nasa and converts brightness into block height. it outputs a code builder script that builds the terain inside minecraft education. the base holds the chemistry blocks , a crafting table and solar panels. reduced gravity is applied with jump and fall effects , so movement feels diferent from earth.

benefits and impact: players pratice chemistry , basic physics and resource planning , and see why recycling and making more from less matters , on mars and on earth. it runs in any classrom or home with minecraft education , needs no coding , and works for kids and adults.

tools: minecraft education , code builder (javascript) , pyhton with the pillow libary , and nasa mola elevation data.

what is creative: instead of only describing in-situ resource utilizaton , players live it. the engine can load the elevation map of any planet or moon and turn it into a world , and we are developing planet profiles so each world also sets its own gravity , atmosphre and dangers.

factors we considered: acessibility for schools , accuracy of the nasa data , and a clear learning loop. live oxygen and power meters , dust storms and a planat picker are still in development.
